cssReference.note: TWO stylesheets implement this contract, for different audiences. Do not confuse them — they are separate files with separate jobs, and a change to one is not a change to the other.

copyFromKit.audience: a developer starting a screen, who pastes it into their own project
copyFromKit.scope: the full component — head cell, data cell, sort atom, control cells, empty header, inline-edit row, link cell

repoStylesheet.audience: anyone consuming this repo's compiled stylesheet directly
repoStylesheet.scope: head cell and data cell ONLY. Scoped to th/td, so div or ARIA-based table markup gets nothing from it. Header internals (the 24px flex title row with its 4px gap, sort control, required marker and help icon) are deliberately out of scope — they cannot live on a `th` without destroying table layout, and this repo ships no markup to hang a wrapper class on.

It had ZERO height declarations, 4px vertical padding, a zebra-striping rule, border-bottom only, and 14px body type instead of 12px caption. Since every AI tool is instructed to read this repo for component truth, that is the most likely root cause of feature sessions being unable to build tables to the design system.

$meta.readThisFirst: ✅ THE HEADER QUESTION IS SETTLED. The canonical table header is `table_head` 26938:61726, variant 26938:52865 — ruled by the design-system owner on 2026-08-25, who linked that exact node and said it "include all actions what it needed to show and hide example, Sorting, Information etc." `Head / Tiltes for tables` 5865:162 is RETIRED as an alias of it, and `X-Head old` stays formally dead. Build from 26938:61726. Do not re-open this from the fact that the section's own sample layout (27002:78668) still instantiates the retired name — that is a Figma-side cleanup item, not evidence of a live competing component. Three more rulings landed the same day and are all recorded in `ownerRulings` below: padding is 8px inline / 0px block on BOTH cells; the data cell's 30px is a MINIMUM and a long value grows the WHOLE ROW; zebra striping is ruled out entirely. One thing is deliberately still open — cell hover — because the Agency semantic layer has no hover token for a field or table surface to follow. It is deferred to the owner, not invented here.
knownNamespaceDivergences: Text colour: this contract MEASURES field/value-primary on both cells. Both stylesheets bind text/primary instead — identical value (#1E293B) in every theme in the repo, and the correct namespace for a non-field element. The contract's own namingException records the field-token-on-a-header as a defect, so binding text/primary is following the defect note, not ignoring the measurement. Unifying the namespaces is an open owner decision.

Border colour: MEASURED as border/subtle on the head cell and field/border-default on the data cell. Both resolve to #E2E8F0. The repo stylesheet now binds each cell the namespace it was measured with, so it does not pre-empt openTokenDecision item 3.

border-radius: the copy-from kit declares var(--border-radius-rounded-none). That name is NOT DEFINED in this repo's shipped CSS — the prefix-free name here is --rounded-none. Harmless for a 0 radius, but the same mistake is live on values that matter: button.json:56 and empty-states.json:59/:69/:94 claim --border-radius-rounded and --border-radius-rounded-xl, and a dead var() there means square corners where 4px and 12px were intended. Repo names: --rounded, --rounded-xl. The mapping JSON is wrong, not the CSS.

Density: the ruled 8px padding binds spacing/md, which this repo re-values per density mode (6px compact, 12px comfortable), so TBL-R2's 8px holds only at default density. And swapping type from font-size/body-base to the MEASURED font-size/caption made the table density-invariant, because caption is re-valued by no density mode. Both are unruled and going to the owner.

Verification note, 2026-08-25: an adversarial review of the rewritten repo stylesheet raised 2 BLOCK findings, both about the height mechanism, and both were CONFIRMED by empirical measurement in headless Chrome rather than argument — see geometry.headCell.minHeight.alsoDeclare. Both are fixed in both stylesheets and in this contract. Partial coverage caveat: 7 of the 40 verification agents died on a session limit, all in the browser-correctness lens, so that lens's lower-severity findings were never independently judged.

minHeight.neverUse: a fixed height that clips content. NOTE: this does NOT mean 'never write the `height` property' — that was the previous wording and it was wrong. In the table model `height` IS a floor, so declaring it is what makes the 34px real, and content taller than 34 still grows the row. Do not strip `height: 34px` out of either stylesheet on the strength of this field.
minHeight.note: A FLOOR, not a sum. Ruled 2026-08-25 (TBL-R2): with padding-block 0 the content measures 1+0+24+0+1 = 26px, and min-height 34 holds the cell open past it. The local stylesheet's old '1+4+24+4+1' arithmetic was retired by that ruling. Centred content places the label identically either way, which is why the 4-vs-0 discrepancy went unnoticed for so long.
minHeight.alsoDeclare: height: 34px. THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING DECLARATION. min-height on a display:table-cell box is EXPLICITLY UNDEFINED by CSS 2.1 §10.7 — Blink and WebKit ignore it, Gecko honours it — while §17.5.3 makes a cell's `height` the maximum of specified and content height, i.e. a MINIMUM, in every engine. Measured in headless Chrome on the shipped rules: min-height:34 alone renders 17px (identical to declaring nothing); height:34 renders 34px. So min-height alone left the header SHORTER than its own 30px data rows, inverting the design.

paddingInline.note: CONFIRMED by owner ruling TBL-R2 ("8px left right"). Figma's payload prints a 9px FALLBACK here. The export value of spacing/md is 8. Bind the token; the 9 is a codegen artefact and is not even stable between reads — another read printed 5, then 1.

paddingBlock.note: CONFIRMED by owner ruling TBL-R2 ("0 top bottom"). Figma's payload prints a 1px FALLBACK here; the export value of spacing/none is 0. The local stylesheet bound spacing/sm (4) and was corrected to match on 2026-08-25.

border.note: 1px on ALL FOUR sides. Width is a raw literal; only the colour is tokenised.

frameWidth.note: Layout context, not a constraint. The sample layout uses 200px columns.

minHeight.alsoDeclare: height: 30px — the load-bearing declaration, for the same reason as the head cell: CSS 2.1 §10.7 makes min-height undefined on a table-cell, §17.5.3 makes `height` a floor. ⚠️ CORRECTION to this contract's earlier wording: declaring both does NOT make a real <table> and a div-based table behave identically. That claim was wrong. On a flex or block box `height: 30px` is a FIXED height and CLIPS instead of growing — the opposite of ruling TBL-R3. A div-based build needs min-height only, plus align-items: stretch on the row. Both published stylesheets are scoped to real table elements (th/td and .cs-table__*), so neither covers div-based markup at all.
minHeight.neverUse: a fixed height that clips content
minHeight.note: ⚠️ RULED, NOT MEASURED. Figma currently binds a FIXED height:30 on 26938:52924. Owner ruling TBL-R3 on 2026-08-25 overrides that: 30 is a MINIMUM, a long value grows the cell, and that growth raises the ENTIRE ROW — never one cell independently. Figma is scheduled to be updated to match; see figmaSideChangesRequired.

rowGrowth.value: the row is the growth unit, not the cell
rowGrowth.note: Native in a real <table>: sibling cells stretch to the tallest in the row, so row-level growth needs no extra CSS. For a div-based table, the row needs align-items: stretch. Do NOT give a cell its own independent height.

paddingInline.note: CONFIRMED by owner ruling TBL-R2 ("8px left right"). Fallback printed correctly as 8 here, unlike the head cell. The local stylesheet had NO inline padding on this cell at all — a genuine omission, added 2026-08-25.

paddingBlock.note: CONFIRMED by owner ruling TBL-R2 ("0 top bottom"). Fallback printed correctly as 0 here, unlike the head cell.

truncation.supersedes: MEASURED value on 26938:52924 was: single line, overflow hidden, text-ellipsis, white-space nowrap.
truncation.note: ⚠️ RULED, NOT MEASURED. Owner ruling TBL-R3 requires a value to be able to grow the row, which an ellipsis makes impossible. So the data cell WRAPS (overflow-wrap: break-word) and `white-space: nowrap` must not be restored. Note the header cell KEEPS nowrap — the ruling covered the data cell only and was not widened. The inline-edit field's single-line value also keeps its ellipsis for the same reason.

composition.rule: One 34px head cell per column, above N 30px data cells. Borders are 1px on all four sides of every cell, so adjacent cells double up unless collapsed.
composition.note: The 1px-all-sides border on every cell is worth attention in implementation: without border-collapse or a negative-margin strategy, a table renders 2px internal gridlines. The design does not record which approach is intended.

letterSpacing.note: Binds fonts/tracking/X-tracking-0 — legacy name absent from the export. Correct name: fonts/tracking/tracking-0.

textTransform.note: NO uppercase treatment. The component set renders 'Title' in sentence case. Rendering header labels in CAPS is wrong against the design system — the local stylesheet reaches the same conclusion and verified it three independent ways.

fontSize.note: Figma's payload ALSO emits a raw text-[12px] on the same element, duplicating the token. Bind the token only.

typography.difference: Head and cell share size (12), line-height (16) and family. Only the WEIGHT differs — 500 for the header, 400 for the value.

colourFormula.pattern: The head cell uses surface/* and border/*; the data cell uses field/*. Both text colours use field/value-primary.

headText.note: A FIELD token used for header text — see namingException.

namingException.case: two token namespaces for one border, and field/* used for header text
namingException.detail: The head border binds border/subtle while the data-cell border binds field/border-default. BOTH resolve to #e2e8f0 — identical colour, two different token names, in one component family. Separately, the header's TEXT binds field/value-primary rather than a text/* token, even though the header is not a form field.
namingException.impact: No visual defect. But a generator inferring 'header uses border/*, cell uses field/*' will be right by accident, and a theme change to only one of the two namespaces would split a table's gridlines.

type.note: ONE variant each in Figma (type=Default). No hover, selected, sorted-active, disabled or error state exists on either set. Zebra striping is RULED OUT (TBL-R4) and is not a gap. ⚠ FLAGGED 2026-09-01 on the owner's instruction — he asked whether states were already defined here and said to flag it if not. They are NOT: this contract has never carried a hover, selected or sorted-active state, because nothing exists in Figma to measure and the Agency semantic layer has no hover token for a field or table surface (its only *hover tokens are action/*, toggle, surface/brand and text/links — all wrong layer for a data-cell surface). So this is a genuine DESIGN gap, not a documentation gap: it cannot be closed by writing a contract, only by the states being designed. Raised to Figma AI on C360-44222. Until then, building any of these in code is an invention.

rulings.subject: canonical header
rulings.quote: this is the exact header selection link which include alla ctiosn what it needed to show and hdie example, Sorting, Information etc.
rulings.decision: `table_head` 26938:61726 (variant 26938:52865) is canonical. `Head / Tiltes for tables` 5865:162 is retired as an alias. `X-Head old` is dead.
rulings.effect: Resolves competingHeaderComponents. No geometry changed — both headers measured 34px, so this is a provenance fix, not a visual one.

rulings.subject: padding on both cells
rulings.quote: 8px left right, 0 top bottom and with hug heigh propeties with minimum height of 30px
rulings.decision: padding-inline = spacing/md (8) and padding-block = spacing/none (0), on the head cell AND the data cell. Height hugs content above the stated minimum.
rulings.effect: CONFIRMS live Figma. CORRECTS the local stylesheet, which bound spacing/sm (4) vertically on the head cell, and which had NO inline padding on the data cell at all. Also retires the old '1+4+24+4+1 = 34' arithmetic: 34 is a floor over 26px of content, not a sum.

rulings.subject: data cell height and growth
rulings.quote: yes, It can increase but this will increase the entire row height not a cell independently. The minium heigh is 30px
rulings.decision: 30px is a MINIMUM. A long value grows the cell, and that growth raises the entire row — never one cell on its own.
rulings.effect: Overrides the measured FIXED height:30 and the measured ellipsis truncation on 26938:52924. In a real <table> the row-level behaviour is native: `height` on a table-cell is treated as a minimum and siblings stretch to the tallest. The actual blocker was `white-space: nowrap`, which stopped the text wrapping so nothing could grow — removed. Figma must be updated to match; see figmaSideChangesRequired.

rulings.subject: zebra striping
rulings.quote: one thign i am sure, Zebra we are not following
rulings.decision: No zebra striping. Rows are not alternately shaded.
rulings.effect: This is a DECISION, not a gap. Stop logging it as a missing state.

rulings.subject: column width bands
rulings.quote: So let me defien here and same must be complied on Golabal (universal) html and css rules. A- column-size=L (this will be default) Minimum width 140px, max width 240px. B- column-size=M : Minimum width 80px, max width 140px. C- column-size=XL : Minimum width 240px, max width 400px.
rulings.decision: Three column-width bands, named to match a Figma variant property `column-size`: M = 80-140px, L = 140-240px (THE DEFAULT), XL = 240-400px. Every column fills within its band; only M and XL need declaring.
rulings.effect: See the new columnWidths section. This SUPERSEDES the previous three bands in Universal Html Rules/02-components/table.css [CS-TBL-14] (generic 80-160, wide 120-240, longform 120-400) on both naming AND values, and moves the DEFAULT up a size — from the smallest band to the middle one, a +60px jump in the default minimum. Nothing in the GitHub repo defined column widths at all before this; the only prior mention was geometry.composition.sampleColumnWidth (200px), explicitly marked 'layout context, not a constraint'.

rulings.subject: density and padding
rulings.quote: The table padding is already managed though varaibles and variable change with Density mdoes change.
rulings.decision: Table padding is DENSITY-AWARE BY DESIGN. Binding spacing/md is correct precisely because that token is re-valued per density mode. The ruled 8px is the DEFAULT-density value, and it becoming 6px at compact / 12px at comfortable is intended behaviour, not drift.
rulings.effect: CLOSES the density question raised against TBL-R2 — that question was posed as 'the ruled 8px only holds at default density', framed as a possible weakening of the ruling. It is not a weakening; it is the mechanism working. Do not hardcode 8px to 'protect' the ruling — that would break density. ⚠ PARTIAL: this ruling addresses PADDING only. The separate type-scale half is still open — see notVerified.

columnWidths.status: RULED 2026-09-01 by the design-system owner (TBL-R5). NEW to this repo — no column-width guidance existed here before.
columnWidths.namingRationale: The band names M / L / XL deliberately match a Figma variant property called `column-size`, so a designer and a developer say the identical word. In CSS the size is declared as a data attribute (`data-column-size="M|L|XL"`) rather than a BEM class, because this design system already uses data attributes for variant axes (data-theme, data-density) and BEM classes for structural modifiers — a column's size is a variant axis.

M.useFor: short values — numbers, phone numbers, dates, tags, chips, short codes, statuses

L.useFor: names, locations, address line 1, and other single-line values that routinely run long
L.note: THE DEFAULT. A column with no declared size gets this band.

columnWidths.fillIsDefault: Every column fills within its band (flex: 1 1 auto + the band as min/max width). A column that must NOT grow has to say so explicitly; silence means fill.
columnWidths.bandsAreContiguous: 80-140-240-400 — the three bands now tile without overlapping. The superseded bands overlapped (80-160, 120-240, 120-400), which meant two of them could both be defensible for the same column.
columnWidths.consequenceToExpect: ⚠ The default moved UP a size. The old default was the smallest band (80px min); the new default is L (140px min), so any column carrying no explicit size gains a 60px larger minimum. On a table that previously just fitted its viewport this can push it into horizontal scroll. Nothing breaks — [CS-TBL-13] handles the scroll correctly, with the first and last columns staying frozen — but a table that used to sit still will start scrolling. Re-check existing banded tables after adopting this.
columnWidths.actionsColumnExempt: The Actions column is NOT banded. It is sized by its controls, carries no title, and [CS-TBL-13] already governs it (frozen right, absorbs slack).
columnWidths.truncationIsMandatory: A banded column can still hit its max, so every cell that can overflow MUST ellipsise AND expose its full value on hover. Note `text-overflow: ellipsis` is INERT on a flex container — the text becomes an anonymous flex item and the property has nothing to act on — so the ellipsis must live on a real inner element. This shipped as a defect twice, in two different tables.
columnWidths.cssReference: Universal Html Rules/02-components/table.css [CS-TBL-14], updated the same day. The retired class names .cs-table__col--wide / --longform are kept there as DEPRECATED aliases so the one existing consumer does not break silently; the mapping is not lossless (--longform's min goes 120 -> 240).
